notes.X1: The causal spine is fully legible: a man senses something wrong, is pulled out, trained, tested, and awakens to reshape the world.
notes.X2: World-building appears only where it drives action—the pod-field, Zion, and the 'farmed for power' reveal land in s03 exactly when Neo needs the truth.
notes.X3: Every entity enters in context: Trinity at the 'white rabbit,' Agent Smith at capture, Morpheus after the pills, Cypher at the betrayal.
notes.X4: Each plot thread pays off—the Oracle's warning, Trinity's faith, and Smith's dominance all return structurally in s06–s07.
notes.X5: Clean three-act hero's-journey shape: ordinary world, descent into truth, death-and-rebirth apotheosis, all proportioned correctly.
notes.X6: Jargon ('Matrix,' 'red/blue pill,' 'the One') is always glossed in-scene rather than dumped.
notes.X7: Crisp, parallel phrasing and strong verbs carry momentum; each beat is self-contained and easy to track.
notes.X8: Neo's doubt and self-doubt make him relatable, and his choice to risk everything for Morpheus is the open-heart turn.
notes.X9: Themes of belief, freedom vs. comfortable illusion, and love-as-resurrection are woven through the plot, not bolted on.
